About.Tagline: DualSense haptics and adaptive triggers, wirelessly.
Adapter.AdviceDistance: Keep the controller within a few metres and test again; if nothing changes, try a Bluetooth 5 or newer adapter.
Adapter.AdvicePlacement: Move the adapter to a front USB 2.0 port or onto a short USB extension cable on the desk, away from USB 3.0 (blue) ports and 2.4 GHz devices such as wireless mouse, keyboard and headset receivers.
Adapter.AdviceRetry: Make sure the controller is on and within a few metres of the adapter, then run the test again.
Adapter.AllGood: {rate} reports/s, next to no loss, no stalls. Suitable for haptics and triggers.
Adapter.FrequentStalls: Frequent stalls: 1% of reports are delayed by more than {stallMs} ms.
Adapter.HapticsBehind: The haptics stream can't keep up ({rate}/s; {target} needed).
Adapter.HapticsStruggling: The haptics stream barely keeps up ({rate}/s).
Adapter.HeadlineBorderline: Borderline: it works, but expect some delay or choppy vibration now and then.
Adapter.HeadlineIncomplete: The measurement is incomplete: the controller stopped sending during the test (it slept, turned off or moved away).
Adapter.HeadlineNoData: Could not measure: no data came from the controller.
Adapter.HeadlineSuitable: Suitable: fast enough for haptics and triggers.
Adapter.HeadlineUnsuitable: Not suitable: you may feel delay and choppy vibration.
Adapter.LongGaps: Controller data stopped for a long moment {gaps, plural, one {# time} other {# times}}.
Adapter.MeasuredGaps: {gaps, plural, one {# gap} other {# gaps}} longer than {ms} ms
Adapter.NeedGaps: fewer than {count} in {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}}
Adapter.OccasionalStalls: Occasional stalls: 1% of reports are delayed by more than {stallMs} ms.
Adapter.RateLow: Controller data arrives slowly ({rate} reports/s; 250 or more is good).
Adapter.RateTooLow: Controller data arrives far too slowly ({rate} reports/s; at least 250 needed).
Adapter.SlowsUnderLoad: Controller data slows down a lot while haptics play ({idleRate} → {loadRate} reports/s).
Adapter.TestRunning: Testing the adapter, this takes about 10 seconds…
Ago.Days: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} ago
Audio.DeviceNotChanged: Windows did not change the default device.
Audio.DevicesUnavailable: The default device can't be changed from here on this Windows; use the Windows sound settings.
Audio.DevicesUnavailableShort: Sound devices can't be picked here.
Audio.HapticsHint: Makes haptics from the game's sound; for games without DualSense support.
Audio.HapticsRumbleNote: The game's own rumble still comes through; it is set on the left.
Audio.HapticsSensitivityHint: How quiet a sound can be and still become haptics. Lower it if background sound keeps the controller rumbling.
Audio.HapticsStatusNative: The Game's Own Haptics In Use
Audio.InputHint: The microphone games and chat apps hear (the Windows default microphone). The controller's mic button switches this microphone.
Audio.OutputHint: Where your PC's sound plays (the Windows default output).
Auto.LowPower: Switch To Low Power Below 20% Battery
Auto.LowPowerHint: When the battery drops below 20% while not charging, Low Power turns on once. If you turn it off, it stays off until the battery is above 20% again.
Auto.StartBridgeHint: The virtual controller starts by itself when the app opens and when the controller connects again. If you stop it, it stays stopped until the controller connects again.
Auto.StartBridgeShort: Starts with the app and on reconnect.
Back.ToGameTip: Hides the app and brings {game} to the front.
Bridge.AttachFailed: The virtual controller could not be plugged into Windows
Bridge.CaptureInvalid: The controller identity file could not be read
Bridge.ControllerLost: The controller disconnected; waiting for it to come back
Bridge.ControllerOpenFailed: The controller could not be opened
Bridge.DetailRunning: The game sees a wired controller; haptics and triggers are relayed.
Bridge.DetailWaiting: The virtual wired controller is plugged in. Start a game.
Bridge.NoCapture: No controller identity: connect the controller by cable and capture it once
Bridge.RowHint: Stop it to hand the controller to another program. With automatic start on, it starts again when the controller reconnects.
Bridge.RowShort: Stop it to free the controller.
Bridge.StatusRunning: The virtual controller is running: games see a wired controller.
Bridge.Watchdog: The virtual controller stopped responding and was restarted
Button.RemappingHint: Choose which button each physical button sends to the game. The ø button can't be remapped.
Cable.ModeHint: Use The Cable: while the cable is in, input, triggers, light, haptics, speaker and microphone go over USB and Bluetooth is disconnected; after unplugging, press the ø button to reconnect. If anything misbehaves choose Charge Only: the cable only charges and everything stays on Bluetooth.
Cable.ModeLabel: When The Cable Is Plugged In
Cable.ModeShort: While the cable is in, the app runs the controller over it and disconnects Bluetooth.
Cable.ModeShortChargeOnly: The cable only charges; the controller stays on Bluetooth.
Calibration.NotEnoughData: Not enough data arrived. Make sure the controller is connected and try again.
Calibration.SticksMoved: The sticks moved. Try again without touching them.
Cannot.StartHidHide: Install HidHide first; without it games see two controllers.
Cannot.StartNoRadio: The virtual controller needs a Bluetooth adapter.
Cannot.StartNotPaired: Pair the controller with Windows first.
Cannot.StartUsb: The virtual controller isn't needed while the controller is on a cable.
Cannot.TestNoController: Connect the controller over Bluetooth to test it.
Classic.RumbleCardHint: General profile: used with the Xbox and DS4 types, or when a game sends only classic rumble.
Connection.BluetoothOffReason: Bluetooth is off. Turn it on in Windows settings.
Connection.BluetoothReason: The controller is connected over Bluetooth.
Connection.NeverPairedReason: No DualSense is paired with Windows. Hold Create and the ø button until the light blinks, then pair it.
Connection.NoRadioReason: No Bluetooth adapter was found on this PC.
Connection.PairedNotConnectedReason: The controller is paired but off or asleep. Press the ø button to turn it on.
Connection.UsbReason: The controller is connected by cable; games already see it as wired, so the virtual controller isn't needed. Unplug it to play wirelessly.
Controller.ForgetConnectedTip: A connected controller can't be forgotten; turn it off first.
Controller.ForgetTip: Removes this controller's name and its own profile choice; it shows up as new when it connects again.
Controller.Intro: Test your controller and fix what you see right away. Stick, trigger and button settings are here too.
Controller.SelectorHelp: This page shows and tests the selected controller.
Controllers.Hint: Controllers you connected stay here. You can give any of them a name; it shows everywhere.
Custom.TriggerHint: The chosen effect stays on this trigger whatever the game sends. Game's Effect leaves the game's own effect.
Custom.TriggerTryHint: Plays both triggers' custom effects for a moment.
Custom.TriggerTryShort: Plays the custom effects on the controller for a moment.
Desktop.AutoOff: Turn Off When a Game Starts
Desktop.AutoOffHint: Mouse mode turns itself off when a game from the list comes to the front or the game in front uses the controller (vibration, trigger effects).
Desktop.AutoOffShort: Turns off when a game comes to the front or uses the controller.
Desktop.ButtonsNote: Touchpad, the ø button and Mute stay as they are.
Desktop.ModeHint: While on, the controller is a mouse and keyboard in Windows; games get no input from it meanwhile. ø + Options turns it on and off too; opening the app with the ø button or pressing the touchpad twice while the app is in front turns it on.
Desktop.ModeShort: Acts as mouse and keyboard; games get no input.
Desktop.OffGameBody: Mouse Mode off, controller in game.
Desktop.OffGameStartedBody: Controller is back in the game.
Desktop.OnBody: The controller is a mouse now.
Desktop.PointerStickHint: The chosen stick moves the pointer; the other one scrolls.
Desktop.RightClickHint: Which touchpad press right clicks. Off: every press is a left click.
Desktop.TouchpadHint: Touchpad: one finger moves the pointer, two fingers up/down scroll; {clicks}. ø + Options turns mouse mode on and off.
Desktop.TouchpadHint.Off: tap or press to left click
Desktop.TouchpadHint.RightSide: tap to left click; press the left half to left click, the right half to right click
Desktop.TouchpadHint.TwoFingers: tap or press with one finger to left click, with two to right click
Diagnostics.Failed: Could not create the diagnostics file: {detail}
Download.GameImagesHint: Game pictures not already on this PC are downloaded from Steam and stored only on this PC. When off, only the pictures in your Steam library and the icons of games you added are shown.
Dsx.ModSupportHint: Game mods made for DSX send trigger effects, the light bar and the player lights from inside this PC; with this on they reach your controller. When the mod resets or closes, everything goes back. It does not work while DSX itself is running.
Dsx.ModSupportShort: Takes trigger and light commands from game mods made for DSX.
Dsx.Status.ActiveMinutes: Listening on port {port}; last message from a mod {minutes} min ago.
Dsx.Status.ActiveSeconds: Listening on port {port}; last message from a mod {seconds} s ago.
Dsx.Status.Failed: Could not open port {port}; not listening.
Dsx.Status.PortInUse: Port {port} is in use (DSX may be running); not listening.
Edge.PaddlesHint: Assign a DualSense button to each back paddle. The Fn buttons are reserved for later use.
Editing.ProfileTip: These settings are saved to this profile. On the Games page you can pick a profile for each game.
Export.DiagnosticsHint: A file to attach to bug reports.
Fallback.StrengthHint: How strong the fallback effect feels.
Fallback.TriggerHint: Used when the game sends no trigger effect.
Force.CloseQuestion: The game is still open. Close it by force?
Game.EffectsCardHint: How strong the haptics and trigger effects sent by DualSense games feel.
Game.FoldersHint: Steam, Epic Games, GOG and the Games folders on your drives are searched by themselves. If your games are somewhere else, add their folder.
Game.HapticsHint: Strength of the game's haptics. Recommended: 150%.
Game.LightOffXbox: With the Xbox 360 type, games can't change the light.
Game.ListAdded: {added, plural, one {# new game} other {# new games}} added
Game.ListHint: Listed, found and added games are recognised when they start. You can pick a controller type and profile for each.
Game.ListInfo.Updated: {count, plural, one {# game} other {# games}} · updated {date}
Game.ListOffline: the server couldn't be reached, check your internet connection.
Game.ListTimeout: the server didn't answer in time.
Game.ListUnsupported: the list is too new for this version, update the app.
Game.OwnSettingsHint: Gives this game a profile named after it; changes affect only this game.
Game.PanelChainTitle: From The Game To The Controller
Game.ProfileTip: The profile that becomes active when this game is recognised
Game.ResetToDefaultHint: The game uses the Default profile again; its own profile is kept.
Game.UsesDefaultProfile: This game uses the Default profile.
Gate.PlotCaption: Sound over the threshold becomes haptics.
Gyro.AimingHint: Turning the controller moves the right stick; it adds to the real right stick.
Gyro.CalibrationHint: Put the controller on a flat surface and keep it still for 2 seconds; the gyro's drift is measured and removed.
Gyro.CalibrationResultText.Moved: The controller moved. Try again without moving it.
Gyro.CalibrationResultText.NoData: No gyro data arrived. Make sure the virtual controller is running and try again.
Gyro.OffsetHint: The blue dot is the offset the gyro adds to the right stick.
Gyro.TargetHint: With Mouse, the gyro moves the Windows pointer and leaves the right stick alone; for games that take mouse and controller together.
Gyro.ToggleHint: When on, each press turns the gyro on or off.
Haptics.Intro: Game haptics can feel weak over Bluetooth; raise the level here.
Health.AdapterNeverTested: The adapter hasn't been tested yet.
Health.AdapterNoData: The last test couldn't measure anything. Try again.
Health.BridgeStuck: The controller is there, but the virtual controller can't reach it. Try reconnecting.
Health.BridgeWaiting: The virtual controller is waiting for the real controller.
Health.DriverMissing: usbip-win2 isn't installed; the virtual controller can't run without it.
Health.DriverServiceMissing: usbip-win2 is installed but its driver service is missing. Reinstall it.
Health.HidingActive: The real controller is hidden from other apps.
Health.HidingAppNotAllowed: The app couldn't be added to the HidHide allow list. Restart the virtual controller.
Health.HidingDriverMissing: HidHide is installed but its driver is missing. Reinstall it.
Health.HidingMissing: HidHide isn't installed; the virtual controller won't start without it, or games would see two controllers.
Health.HidingNotHidden: The real controller couldn't be hidden; games may see two controllers.
Health.HidingReady: HidHide is ready; the real controller is hidden while the virtual controller runs.
Health.RestartPending: Restart the PC to finish the installation.
Health.SteamOff: Steam Input is off; haptics and triggers reach the game.
Health.SteamOnForApp: Steam Input is on for this game; it can block native haptics.
Health.SteamOnGlobally: Steam Input is on for PlayStation controllers; it can block native haptics.
Health.SteamUnknown: The Steam Input setting couldn't be read.
Hero.BatteryChargingTip: The controller's battery level; it is charging now.
Hid.HideActive: The real controller is hidden from games.
Hid.HideHideFailed: Could not hide the real controller: {detail}
Hid.HideNoAppPath: Could not determine the application's file path.
Hid.HideNotInstalled: HidHide is not installed. Games may also see the real Bluetooth controller (double input).
Hid.HideRestoreFailed: Could not restore HidHide settings; will retry on next start: {detail}
Hide.GameTip: Not a game? Take it off the list
Hiding.Failed: The controller could not be hidden: {detail}
Hiding.Unavailable: The virtual controller didn't start: HidHide isn't installed. Install it from the Setup page.
Hint.PressPs: Press the ø button, or pair it if this is the first time.
Idle.PowerOffHint: Minutes idle before notice or power-off (0 = never).
Idle.Timeout: The controller has not been used for {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}
Info.Hint: Read from the controller itself; the address is shortened for privacy.
Info.Short: Read from the controller; address shortened.
Info.Title: Controller Info
Installed.AddHint: Can't find your game? Add it with Add Game.
Installed.Empty: No games were found on this PC.
Keep.InTrayHint: The icon stays in the hidden icons area next to the clock.
Keep.InTrayShort: Its icon stays next to the clock.
Language.Label: Language
Latency.Hint: Extra delay of the Bluetooth link: median / worst 1%. Measured while the virtual controller runs.
Latency.Value: Link delay {p50} ms (worst {p99} ms), relay {relay} ms
Light.FromGameHint: If the game sends a colour, it is shown; if not, or when this is off, your light is shown.
Light.Intro: If a game sends its own colour, that colour is used.
Light.ModeBatteryHint: Green, amber and red show the battery level; under 10% red pulses.
Light.ModeBreathingHint: Your colour slowly dims and brightens again.
Light.ModeRainbowHint: The light bar slowly cycles through the colour wheel.
Light.ModeStaticHint: The light bar stays on in the colour you choose.
Light.OffLowPower: The light is off while Low Power is on.
Link.AdviceBorderline: Some delay now and then: move the controller closer to the adapter.
Link.AdvicePoor: You can feel the delay: move closer, bring the adapter forward on a USB extension cable, away from 2.4 GHz devices.
Link.GraphTip: The last 60 seconds. Coloured area: the worst delay of each second; thin line: the typical delay. Above the dashed line you can feel it; the small ticks below mark seconds with lost reports or a pause.
Live.Idle: Shows here while the virtual controller runs.
Live.LeftHapticsTip: The vibration going to the controller's left haptic motor right now.
Live.PreviewNeedsBridge: The live preview shows while the virtual controller is running.
Live.RightHapticsTip: The vibration going to the controller's right haptic motor right now.
Live.SignalsTip: The last 10 seconds: how far the triggers are pressed, the vibration going to the haptic motors and the microphone level.
Live.Speaker: Speaker
Live.Title: Live
Live.TriggerTip: How far you are pressing the trigger.
Look.ChangeTip: Choose how this controller is drawn in the app.
Look.EdgeNote: The colours are for the standard controller; you can give this one your own image.
Look.FileTitle: Choose A Picture For The Controller
Look.ImageFailed: That file could not be read as a picture.
Look.Label: Controller Colour
Look.OwnHint: PNG, JPG or WebP. It is drawn as it is, without the light or pressed buttons on it.
Look.PickerHint: Only changes the drawing in the app; each controller keeps its own choice.
Look.RemoveTip: Deletes your own image; the controller goes back to the default drawing.
Low.PowerNote: Haptics, light and sound are reduced; the battery lasts longer.
Low.PowerOffNote: While Low Power is on, the light, speaker and microphone are off.
Mic.ButtonHint: The controller's microphone shows up in games like the wired one. The mic button on the controller turns it on and off; while the button glows orange the microphone is on.
Mic.ButtonModeHint: What the controller's mic button and the Microphone tile in Quick Settings do. Either way the button's light goes out, games and chat apps hear silence, and the Controller Microphone stays in Windows. Mute: the controller keeps sending sound; press again and it's back at once; it is not muted any more after the app restarts. Turn Off: the controller stops sending sound and Pass Microphone to Games turns off (and stays off); press again to turn it back on. If a PC microphone is the Windows default, the button mutes it in both modes.
Mic.ButtonModeShort: Either way games hear nothing. Mute comes back at once; Turn Off shuts the controller mic down.
Mic.NoiseGateHint: Cuts background noise while you're quiet.
Mic.SendShort: The mic is on while its button glows orange.
Notifications.ShowHint: Small cards in the bottom-right corner.
Notify.BatteryHint: At 20% and 10%, and when fully charged.
Notify.CableBody: The controller now works over its cable and the virtual controller was stopped. It starts again by itself when Bluetooth is back.
Notify.ConnectionHint: When a controller connects or drops.
Notify.ErrorsHint: When it stops on a problem, with the reason.
Notify.GameHint: When a known game starts and when the controller type changes.
Notify.GameListBody: {added, plural, one {# new game} other {# new games}} added
Notify.HidHideHint: If the virtual controller can't start because HidHide isn't installed.
Notify.HidHideShort: When it can't start without HidHide.
Notify.LinkHint: If the link stays weak long enough to feel the delay, once each time.
Notify.LinkShort: When the link stays weak for a while.
Notify.PowerOffHint: When it turns off for being idle.
Notify.TrayBody: Find the icon by the clock
Other.GamesRumbleTryHint: Plays a short rumble with these settings; Left and Right Haptics try one side only.
Other.GamesTriggerTryHint: Puts the chosen effect on L2 and R2 for a moment.
Overview.Intro: At-a-glance status of your controller, the virtual controller and settings.
Overview.Subtitle: When started, games see the Bluetooth controller as a wired one.
Pad.ChoiceAutoLine: Each game uses its own choice; without one, the best controller for the game.
Pad.ModeDualSenseBody: The controller appears as a DualSense again.
Pad.SwapRestartHint: If the game does not see the controller, restart the game.
Pad.ToastPendingBody: Applies when you restart the game.
Pad.TypeAutoDefaultLine: Picks the best controller for the game; for a game we know nothing about, uses the Default Controller Type.
Pad.TypeAutoLine: Picks The Best Controller For The Game
Pad.TypeDefaultHint: Used for games we know nothing about.
Pad.TypeDeferred: Applies When You Restart The Game
Pad.TypeDeferredHint: If the controller type changes while the game is open, the game may lose the controller.
Pad.TypeDualSenseLine: Everything works: the game's haptics, triggers, light, speaker and microphone.
Pad.TypeDualShock4Line: For older games that only know the PS4 controller: rumble and light work; no adaptive triggers, game haptics or speaker.
Pad.TypeGameHint: The controller this game sees. If unsure, leave it on Automatic.
Pad.TypeXboxLine: For games that don't know PlayStation controllers at all: rumble only; no touchpad or motion sensor either.
Pad.TypeXboxSeriesLine: For games made for Xbox controllers: rumble works; no touchpad or motion sensor.
Page.HapticsTriggersIntro: The game's own effects pass through; where it sends none, Xbox And DS4 Rumble takes over.
Pause.HapticsInSilenceHint: Sends no haptics to the controller while the game is silent; saves battery and CPU, the first hit after silence may come a few ms later.
Pause.HapticsInSilenceShort: No haptics are sent while the game is silent.
Player.LedsHint: The small LEDs below the touchpad.
Player.LedsPatternHint: The LEDs below the touchpad: a player number or all of them.
Power.OffFailed: Could not turn off the controller. Hold the ø button for 10 seconds to turn it off.
Power.OffIdle: The controller was turned off after {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} without use.
Power.OffWhenIdleHint: When on, turns off the controller once the idle time has passed.
Power.OffWhenIdleShort: Power off the controller when idle time is up.
Present.AsEdgeHint: When off, games see a standard DualSense; for games that only know the DualSense. Takes effect on the next connection.
Profile.DefaultNote: Used for games without a profile and when no game runs
Profile.Games: {count, plural, one {Used by # game} other {Used by # games}}
Profile.ImportFailed: This file is not a profile file.
Profile.Label: Profile
Profile.SharedByGames: Settings are shared with other games using this profile.
Profiles.Hint: A profile keeps the haptics and triggers, sticks/triggers, remap, gyro and light (effects included) settings together. Your changes are saved to the active profile. On the Games page you can pick a profile for each game; games without one use Default.
Profiles.Short: Keeps stick, trigger, remap and light settings.
Protect.DefaultAudioHint: If Windows switches your PC's speaker or microphone to the controller by itself when the virtual controller starts, the previous one is put back. If you make the controller the default on purpose in the Windows sound settings, that is left alone.
Protect.DefaultAudioShort: Switches back if Windows picks the controller.
Ps.OpenAppHint: A short ø button press brings DS5 Untethered to the front with Mouse Mode on; another press sends it back to the icon next to the clock. "Also In Games" decides what happens while a game is open. A long press always goes to the game. Works while the virtual controller is running.
Ps.OpenAppInGamesHint: On: in a game, a short ø button press brings the app up and the press does not reach the game; another press hides the app and brings the game back. Off: in a game, the ø button goes to the game.
Ps.OpenAppInGamesShort: A short ø button press opens the app in games too.
Ps.OpenAppShort: With no game open, a short ø button press shows the app.
Quick.HapticsTip: Sets how strong the haptics sent by the game feel.
Quick.InputTip: The microphone games and chat apps hear. The mic button and the Microphone tile switch this microphone.
Quick.LightTip: Sets the brightness of the controller's light bar.
Quick.LowPowerShort: On · haptics, light and sound reduced
Quick.LowPowerTip: Softens haptics and triggers, turns the light and sound off and powers the controller off sooner when idle, so the battery lasts longer.
Quick.MicButtonTip: Either way the light goes out and games hear silence. Mute: the controller keeps sending sound, back at once. Turn Off: the controller stops sending sound and Pass Microphone to Games turns off.
Quick.MicOffInSettingsTip: The controller microphone is off in Settings > Audio. Turn it on there to use it.
Quick.MicTileTip: Click to mute or unmute the selected microphone, like the controller's mic button.
Quick.MicTip: Makes the controller's microphone available to games, like on a wired controller.
Quick.MouseModeTip: Move and click the Windows mouse pointer with the controller; games get no input from it meanwhile.
Quick.OutputTip: Where your PC's sound plays. Pick the Controller Speaker to send all sound to the controller.
Quick.OverriddenByLowPower: While Low Power is on, Low Power sets this.
Quick.ProfileTip: Switches between saved settings profiles; the chosen one applies right away.
Quick.ShortcutsTip: Hold the ø button and press another button to change the profile, haptics strength, DualSense Mode and more from the controller.
Quick.SpeakerTip: Plays the sounds the game sends to the controller's speaker; works only with the DualSense type.
Quick.TriggerTip: Sets how hard the adaptive triggers push back.
Quiet.WhilePlayingHint: Silent in games and full screen apps.
Reason.ControllerOff: The controller is off or not paired.
Reason.UsbOnly: The controller is on a USB cable.
Reconnect.Hint: Closes the connection to the controller and opens it again; Bluetooth stays connected.
Remap.Intro: Buttons, sticks and gyro change inside the DualSense report, so the game's haptics and trigger effects keep working.
Rumble.FeelHint: Soft: low, smooth tones. Punchy: higher, shorter, sharper hits.
Rumble.Hint: The game's rumble plays as haptics on the controller.
Setup.AdapterInstructions: A short test measures whether your Bluetooth adapter carries haptics and trigger data fast enough. Keep the controller close during the test.
Setup.ControllerMissing: No DualSense is connected over Bluetooth.
Setup.ControllerOnUsb: The controller is connected with a USB cable. Unplug it and connect over Bluetooth.
Setup.DriversInstructions: DS5 Untethered needs two free drivers: usbip-win2 for the virtual wired controller and HidHide to hide the real controller from games. Download both from their official pages, install them, then check again.
Setup.HidHideMissing: HidHide is not installed (or its driver is missing).
Setup.LanguageInstructions: Choose the app language. You can change it later in the settings.
Setup.PageIntro: What DS5 Untethered needs to work. Complete the missing steps, then check again.
Setup.PairInstructions: With the controller off, hold the ø button and Create together until the light bar flashes quickly, then let go. Then add the controller with "Add device" in the Windows Bluetooth settings.
Setup.RadioMissing: No Bluetooth adapter was found on this computer.
Setup.RadioOff: Bluetooth is off. Turn it on in the Windows settings.
Setup.RestartFailed: Windows couldn't start the restart. You can restart the computer from the Start menu.
Setup.RestartPending: You may need to restart the computer for the drivers to work.
Setup.RestartQuestion: Restart the computer now? Open programs will be closed, so save your work first.
Setup.UsbIpMissing: usbip-win2 is not installed (or its driver is missing).
Shortcut.DoesProfile: Previous / next profile (the player LEDs show its number)
Shortcuts.Hint: Hold the ø button and press one of the buttons below. During a shortcut the game doesn't see the ø button or the button used; in a game, a plain short ø button press still reaches the game.
Shortcuts.Short: Hold the ø button and press one of the listed buttons.
Speaker.OffLowPower: The speaker is off while Low Power is on.
Speaker.OffPadType: The speaker doesn't work with the {type} type.
Speaker.SendGameAudioHint: Game audio goes to the controller's speaker or headphone jack; works only with the DualSense type
Speaker.SwitchHint: Plays the sounds the game sends to the controller's speaker; works only with the DualSense type.
Star.Label: Star
Start.FileHint: Play opens this file: the game's exe or a shortcut.
Start.WithWindowsHint: Starts in the background when you sign in, without opening the window.
Start.WithWindowsShort: Starts in the background when you sign in.
State.CableOnlyText: The Bluetooth link was lost; games see the wired controller directly. It starts again by itself when Bluetooth is back.
State.NotConnectedText: Once it connects, the virtual controller starts by itself and games see a wired controller.
State.VirtualOffText: The controller is connected over Bluetooth. Press Start Virtual Controller and games see it as a wired controller.
State.WaitingText: The virtual controller is on and waiting. Turn the controller on with the ø button: it connects by itself and games see a wired controller.
Steam.InputAdvice.NotInstalled: Steam is not installed; no Steam Input conflict.
Steam.InputAdvice.Off: Steam Input is off; DS5 Untethered's controller reaches the game directly.
Steam.InputAdvice.OnForApp: Steam Input is on for this game. Haptics and trigger effects may be lost. To turn it off: in the Steam library, right-click the game > Properties > Controller > "Disable Steam Input".
Steam.InputAdvice.OnGlobally: PlayStation controller support is on in Steam. Steam Input may replace the controller with its own virtual pad, and haptics and trigger effects are lost. To turn it off for the game: in the Steam library, right-click the game > Properties > Controller > "Disable Steam Input".
Steam.InputAdvice.Unknown: Could not read the Steam Input setting. If haptics don't work in a game launched from Steam, right-click the game > Properties > Controller > "Disable Steam Input".
Support.Label: Support

Test.NoController: No controller found for the test. Make sure the controller is connected via Bluetooth.

Put the controller down and
leave the sticks for 3 seconds.
Tester.DirectHint: The virtual controller is off, so the controller is only read; nothing is sent to it.
Tester.MotionNeedsFull: Motion and touch data appear once the controller sends full reports.
Tester.NoInputHint: No input from the controller. Make sure it is connected over Bluetooth.
Tester.OutputsHint: Live reading may pause briefly while a test runs.
Tester.StickHint: The grey dot is the raw position, the blue dot what games receive with your settings.

Try.RowHint: Plays on the controller with these settings.
Unsupported.GamesHint: These games use the Xbox And DS4 Rumble settings of the profile you pick.
Update.AutoCheckHint: Looks on GitHub for a new version at start and once a week. Only a file is requested; nothing about you is sent.
Update.CheckInvalid: Couldn't check: the version info couldn't be read.
Update.CheckTimeout: Couldn't check: the server didn't answer.
Update.Confirm: Updating stops the virtual controller for a moment.
Update.DownloadOffline: Couldn't download: the connection dropped, try again.
Update.DownloadRejected: The downloaded file was faulty and was deleted. Try again.
Update.LaunchFailed: Setup couldn't be started; close and reopen the app.
Update.NotYetAvailable: The new version isn't ready yet, try again a bit later.
Update.SaveFailed: Couldn't save the file; check the free disk space.
Update.ZipCopy: This copy came from the zip; get the new version from the page.
Xbox.SeriesFallbackBody: Xbox Series couldn't start, using Xbox 360.
Xbox.TriggerGamesHint: These games send trigger rumble with the Xbox Series type.
Xbox.TriggerRumbleSettingHint: When on, games with Xbox trigger rumble see an Xbox Series controller, and with the Xbox Series type the game's trigger rumble plays on the DualSense triggers. When off, the game's trigger rumble is ignored.
Xbox.TriggerRumbleSettingShort: Plays Xbox trigger rumble on the DualSense triggers in games that use it.
